newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria raises power prices, drops fuel prices.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria raises power prices, drops fuel prices.

text.p: Bulgaria's interim government on Monday raised electricity, coal and heating prices but decreased petrol prices effective from April 1 in line with the lev/dollar exchange rate, senior government officials said.
Energy Minister Georgi Stoilov said electricity and coal prices will rise by an average of 30 percent and heating prices will increase by 70 percent.
Petrol prices will fall by between eight and nine percent and diesel prices will drop by 14.9 percent due to the lev's rise against the dollar in March.
Stoilov said the new average electricity price, which includes value added tax, will be 62.56 levs per kilowatt hour (about four cents).

Delayed price rises and the drastic fall of the lev earlier this year have delayed payments of 36 billion levs from the National Electricity Company for nuclear fuel supplies from Russia for the Kozloduy nuclear plant. Consumers owe the company 40 billion levs.
The new chairman of the NEC executive board, Vassil Anastasov, said the company needed 300 billion levs for its normal operation.
"The present prices do not include the necessary sums for the NEC's investment policy and for transportation and storage of nuclear fuel, which total 90 billion levs," Anastasov said.
Funds will be also needed for transporting spent nuclear fuel from the Kozloduy nuclear plant, which would cost Bulgaria some 90 billion levs per year, he added.
Since July, energy prices have been revised each month, mainly according to the inflation rate and the lev/dollar exchange rate.

Petrol prices will drop by between eight and 8.8 percent and diesel prices will fall by 14.9 percent effective from April 1 due to a recent rise of the lev against the dollar in March and a drop of crude prices on the Mediterranean market, the new chairman of the government price committee, Mladen Mladenov, told reporters.
He said the new fuel prices had been calculated at a dollar rate of 1,692 levs.
